observations.text: The provider publishes OAuth server metadata at https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
The metadata lists PKCE code challenge methods: S256.
The metadata advertises a client registration endpoint (https://calendly.com/oauth/register), so apps may be creatable through an API.
observations.note: The agent did not register an app: that would create a real client on your behalf.

observations.text: Client authentication methods at the token endpoint: none.
The authorize endpoint sent an unauthenticated request to a sign-in page (calendly.com/app/login).
observations.how: GET https://calendly.com/oauth/authorize with a made-up client_id (oauth-guide-agent-probe), no login, redirects not followed
observations.note: Sign-in comes before any client check here, so the agent could not see how an unregistered client is treated.

observations.text: The token endpoint rejected an invalid test request with HTTP 401: "invalid_client: Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method.".

observations.how: POST https://calendly.com/oauth/token with a made-up authorization code and client (nothing is created or changed)
observations.note: So it validates the client and code before issuing anything. It asks for client authentication via the WWW-Authenticate header.

observations.text: A request to api.calendly.com with no token is rejected with HTTP 401.
observations.note: So API calls need an access token.
